requirements.requirement: Run a long-running background worker as a managed systemd service named inventory-worker on node1
requirements.summary: Unit file /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service created with an infinite tick-loop ExecStart, verified clean by systemd-analyze verify, enabled and started; systemctl status shows Active: active (running) with the worker and its sleep child in the service cgroup.

requirements.requirement: Service is confined so it writes only inside /var/lib/inventory
requirements.summary: Directory /var/lib/inventory created and owned by the service's dedicated user; unit uses ProtectSystem=strict with ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory (confirmed via systemctl show on the live unit). Only expected files (count, inventory.log) exist there, owned by inventory-worker. A falsification test using a transient unit with identical sandbox directives showed a write to /etc failing (read-only filesystem) while a write to /var/lib/inventory succeeded, corroborating the confinement is actually enforced rather than merely declared. The falsification ran as a separate transient unit rather than the inventory-worker unit itself, which is a minor indirection but uses matching directives.
Unit defines NoNewPrivileges=yes and an empty CapabilityBoundingSet=; systemctl show on the running unit confirms NoNewPrivileges=yes is actually applied.

overall_summary: The executor deployed inventory-worker as a properly confined, enabled, and running systemd service on node1, with directly observed evidence that NoNewPrivileges is applied and that writes are actually restricted to /var/lib/inventory via a falsification test. The independently required node-restart evidence protocol was also completed with a full pre-restart baseline, an acknowledged reboot, a directly observed change in boot identity (636556ce... -> c8000397...), and post-restart confirmation that the service is enabled/active and that its persisted counter/log data survived and continued incrementing. Operational hygiene is high: a failed transient-unit attempt caused no mutation, and the one test artifact created during falsification was promptly cleaned up.
limitations: The confinement falsification test ran against a separate transient systemd-run unit configured with matching sandbox directives rather than against the actual inventory-worker.service unit, so it is strong corroborating evidence rather than a direct test of the deployed service instance.

Restart evidence relies on connectivity gaps (timeouts/connection reset) as an implicit signal the node was down, rather than a direct 'node unreachable' state capture, though the subsequent boot_id change and service recovery are directly observed.

operational_hygiene.summary: Command trace shows a clean, purposeful sequence: user/group creation, data dir, script, unit file, enable/start, and read-only verification, all directly tied to the task. One systemd-run falsification attempt (cmd-84ef636ce88340b6) failed to start (connection reset) and produced no state change. The successful falsification run (cmd-a9f51374a0fb4d82) left a test artifact (/var/lib/inventory/should-succeed) and a transient unit, both of which were explicitly cleaned up immediately afterward (cmd-0ea1e65b024044f8: rm -f should-succeed; systemctl reset-failed inv-test), leaving no residue. The restart protocol used a backgrounded reboot command (cmd-4695f0b789fc4753), a necessary bounded mutation for the independently required node-restart evidence, and left only an expected /tmp/reboot.log artifact. No abandoned files, conflicting services, unsafe exposure, or weakened security controls were observed; after-executor failed-services and package-health checks are clean.
